newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW- French shippers eye quality air service.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- French shippers eye quality air service.

text.p: The French shippers council, the Association des Utilisateurs du Fret (AUTF), says air freight forwarders and airlines are still some way short of providing the quality of service shippers are looking for.

"While forwarders and airlines have become more aware of shippers' requirements, they must work closer to provide an all-in service package," the chairman of the AUTF's air transport commission, Philippe Oddone, told Reuters in an interview.

Oddone said industry-wide standards were vital to the future of airfreight, one example being the regular publication of service standards by airlines, covering such issues as bookings and transit time.

"At present, there is an absence of clear and precise ground rules on the quality of service shippers can expect to receive and establishing a set of criteria makes good sense. However,for quality indicators to have any meaning and value it is necessary they be approved by a recognised industry body such as International Air Transport Association (IATA) or the Assciation of European Airlines (AEA)," Oddone added.

Along with the publication of service standards, Oddone identified bar coding, ground handling, electronic data interchange and security as the main areas were improvements in quality should be made, he said.

The Paris airports air cargo steering committee, (the Comite Interprofessionel du Fret - CIF) which groups forwarders, airlines, customs and the airport authority - was perhaps an ideal forum for debating these and other issues, Oddone added.

"Maybe taking a seat on the air cargo steering committee would be the best way for shippers to get their views across and cementing relations with the different parties working in the sector. It's likely we'd respond positively if an invitation was made," he said.
Oddone said the CIF had an important role to play in anticipating shippers' requirements.

"More and more shippers are looking at European' options for their logistics and distribution systems taking into account the varying degrees of competitiveness of ports and airports in Europe. The CIF's commitment to making Charles de Gaulle(CDG) airport as attractive a gateway as possible for freight is a big step in the right direction."

In recent years, the French shippers council had blamed inadequate infrastructure at CDG for growing air traffic congestion and warned that short of an improvement its members would be obliged, in the economic interest of their firms, to use other airports.
Today, Oddonne says the outlook is brighter following the adoption of a state/airport authority project to build two additional runways at the airport before the turn of the century.
"We support this project because it is a viable, short-term solution and there is a pressing need to create more capacity.

"As for the idea of building all-cargo airports, similar to those of the express distribution groups, this remains a long-term possibility albeit a remote one, as around 75 percent of airfreight is transported on passenger and combi flights." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
